assumptions.claim: All bits of addr_hit must be driven to a known value (ideally zero) by other logic before this always_comb block executes, because no default assignment or else branch is present.
assumptions.cond: On every evaluation of this always_comb block (i.e., every time reg_addr changes)
assumptions.risk: If addr_hit is not fully assigned before this block, simulation and synthesis will infer latches on unassigned bits, preserving stale values. A stale addr_hit could erroneously select a security-critical register (key, wipe, digest), enabling unauthorized read/write and potential secret leakage or failed wipe.

formal.consequent: |(addr_hit) implies exactly one bit is set (or some property of full-case covering) but cannot be expressed locally; relies on external zero default.

uncertain_points.claim: The always_comb block missing a default assignment to addr_hit may infer latches if not complemented by an external default-zero block. The generated netlist may retain previous decode values, leading to multiple addr_hit bits set or phantom register selection.
uncertain_points.cond: When reg_addr does not match any of the listed offsets, or when the external default block is omitted or severed
uncertain_points.risk: Latch-inferred addr_hit can cause simultaneous selection of a key register and a control register, bypassing intended access gating. This could lead to key extraction or unauthorized wipe of secret state.

security_implications: This chunk decodes access to HMAC key registers (HMAC_KEY_0..HMAC_KEY_31), the wipe secret register, and digest registers. A faulty addr_hit due to missing default assignment (inferred latches) can hold stale decode values, causing writes to unintended key slots, bypassing wipe operations, or leaking digest through read mux collapse. Such failures can compromise key confidentiality and integrity, violate zeroization protocols, and defeat access control mechanisms.
